sourceClarifications: 29.26: The edge crossing the field boundary is 40.0 centimetres long, so the partial-overlap emf is 10.0 millivolts.
29.32: The desired potential difference is 1.0 millivolt, confirmed in the source image.
29.40: The specified time is 0.500 microsecond, not millisecond.
29.41: The printed question asks for one sixth of the current. The appendix time of 0.75 second corresponds instead to one sixteenth. The solution follows the printed one-sixth condition.
29.43: The number of windshield wipers is unspecified. The estimate explicitly states two or three wipers, giving 60 or 65 ampere.
29.45: The capacitance is 20 microfarad and both requested times are 200 microsecond.
29.48: The magnetic field points along x. Rotation about x gives zero emf, while rotation about y or an edge parallel to z gives the same nonzero amplitude.
29.58: The y and z components of the magnetic field are negative in the printed vector. The induced potential is higher at end b.
29.60: The capacitance is 10.00 microfarad and the initial charge is 100 microcoulomb. The RC approximation and the distinction between the switching pulse and later decay are stated.
29.63: The requested displacement current is 21 microampere, giving time 5.0 seconds.
